question: A 45-year-old man in respiratory distress presents to the emergency department. He sustained a stab to his left chest and was escorted to the nearest hospital. The patient appears pale and has moderate difficulty with breathing. His O2 saturation is 94%. The left lung is dull to percussion. CXRs are ordered and confirm the likely diagnosis. His blood pressure is 95/57 mm Hg, the respirations are 22/min, the pulse is 87/min, and the temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F). His chest X-ray is shown. Which of the following is the next best step in management for this patient?
analysis: Based on the clinical presentation of a 45-year-old man with respiratory distress, stab wound to the left chest, dullness to percussion on the left lung, and likely diagnosis confirmed on CXR, the next best step in management is to relieve the pneumothorax by inserting a chest tube.
